laura_sales: Quick ask from health-POC netops: preserve client IP for logs, allow TLS inspection, SNI rewrite concerns, and exact egress IPs for their firewall. Can we give short options and a copy/paste allowlist?

andy_netops: Short options:
- VPC peering: preserves src IP end-to-end, needs route updates and cross-account approval.
- PrivateLink: fastest to onboard, typically NATs to endpoint EIP unless you front with a proxy/NLB. Includes endpoint hourly + per-GB fees.

jun_infra: For POC recommend either: 1) PrivateLink + small NLB + reverse-proxy (X-Forwarded-For to preserve client identity), or 2) Peering (native src-IP) if they require IP-based ACLs.

security_ops: If they rewrite SNI or terminate mTLS on the inspection box, cert pinning/mTLS will break. Mitigation: terminate mTLS at their border and use app auth to our API, or request Dedicated for mutual-TLS support.

andy_netops: Allowlist snippet (replace placeholders):
```
# Outbound allowlist for Redwood POC
allow tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP_1> 443
allow tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP_2> 443
allow udp from 10.20.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP_1> 123
```

laura_sales: Perfect. Also need a 1-line cost note for their finance approver for a 2-week test.

andy_netops: 1-line cost note: "PrivateLink adds small hourly endpoint charge + per-GB processing; peering has no endpoint hour fee but may incur data transfer depending on AZ/region; for ~100GB expect O($10-100) in data fees for the POC."

laura_sales: Thanks — I'll send this to their NetOps and SOC.
